item.title: i14 Ports Laplace 3B Linear Attention Model to AWS Trainium2
item.description:
i14 Ports Laplace 3B Linear Attention Model to AWS Trainium2

AI research company i14 has updated the implementation of Laplace 3B, a linear attention alternative to traditional transformer architectures, by bringing the model to AWS Trainium2 using TorchNeuron Native.

💡 Why it matters

Most large language models (LLMs) utilize transformer architectures with softmax attention, which causes the key-value (KV) cache to grow as conversation or document context increases. This growth can lead to:

  • Reduced concurrency
  • Increased serving costs
  • The need for agentic applications to discard useful history

🧩 How it works

Laplace 3B is a 24-layer decoder that replaces softmax attention with Simple Gated Linear Attention (GLA).

  • Linear Attention: Reorganizes computation around a recurrent state updated for each token, changing training attention complexity from O(T2) to O(T).
  • Context Compression: GLA compresses prior context into a fixed-size matrix state.
  • Fixed State: The inference state remains fixed at 29.5 MB per sequence, independent of context length.

⚙️ Key details

Working with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center (GenAIIC), i14 transitioned the model from GPU-optimized Triton kernels to the TorchNeuron Native PyTorch backend. Technical adjustments included:

  • Kernel Optimization: The team replaced the fused_chunk_simple_gla Triton kernel with standard PyTorch operators, using 16 chunks of 128 tokens to match the 128 partitions of the NeuronCore on-chip buffer.
  • Compiler Compatibility: The 16 chunk steps of the GLA recurrence were statically unrolled to fit the on-chip memory limits and graph-size of the compiler.
  • Throughput Improvements: Two all_to_all collectives in MuonFSDP2 increased throughput by 1.63 times and reduced per-rank traffic by 24 times.

Hardware Specifications

Laplace 3B was deployed on a trn2.48xlarge instance, which features:

Component Specification
Chips 16 Trainium2 chips
NeuronCores 64 logical NeuronCores
Connectivity NeuronLink-v3
SBUF 28 MiB State Buffer with 128 partitions per NeuronCore
PSUM 2 MiB partial-sum buffer wired to a 128×128 systolic Tensor Engine

Performance Metrics

On one trn2.48xlarge instance, the model achieved the following:

  • Training Speed: Approximately 120,000 tokens per second.
  • Inference Throughput: 11,544 output tokens per second across 1,280 concurrent sequences.

#AWS #Trainium2 #LinearAttention #LLM #i14

Source: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Deepgram Optimizes Nova-3 Speech-to-Text Model Using AWS Trainium2
item.description:
Deepgram Optimizes Nova-3 Speech-to-Text Model Using AWS Trainium2

Deepgram has collaborated with AWS to port its Nova-3 speech-to-text model to AWS Trainium2 to improve inference efficiency for offline batch workloads, such as medical transcription and contact-center analytics.

⚙️ Key details

Deepgram and the AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team transitioned Nova-3 from standard PyTorch code to AWS Trainium2 using the following process:

  • Initial Porting: Used TorchNeuron, the native PyTorch integration of the Neuron Compiler, supporting both eager execution and torch.compile.
  • Compilation: The model was first run in eager mode to identify CPU fallbacks, then compiled with torch.compile as separate static-shape graphs for the encoder and decoder, resulting in no CPU fallbacks.
  • Accuracy Validation: Numerical accuracy was verified via layer-level output consistency against CPU and end-to-end Word Error Rate (WER).
  • Kernel Optimization: Replaced several layers with fused kernels from the public NKI Library (NKILib), including:
    • Fused QKV projections
    • Fused feed-forward network (FFN) layers
    • Depthwise 1D convolution
  • Infrastructure: The final configuration runs eight model replicas on a single Amazon EC2 trn2.3xlarge instance.

💡 Why it matters

Serving efficiency determines the amount of audio Deepgram can process within a specific infrastructure budget. By utilizing AWS AI chips, Deepgram achieved the following:

  • Cost Efficiency: Processed 11–70 percent more audio per dollar on offline, throughput-oriented batch workloads compared to previous compute options.
  • Scalability: These gains allow Deepgram to scale more efficiently and provide models to customers at lower prices.
  • Customer Benefit: These improvements extend to customers self-hosting Deepgram models in their own virtual private cloud (VPC) on Amazon SageMaker AI.

🚀 Availability

Deepgram models are available through:

  • The Deepgram API
  • Self-hosted environments, including Amazon SageMaker AI

#Deepgram #AWS #Trainium2 #SpeechToText #InferenceOptimization

Source: How Deepgram optimized voice AI at scale with AWS Trainium | Amazon Web Services
